findings.where: Article page specimen: the body paragraphs, the subhead 'So, what are the key chapter topics?', the numbered list and the closing paragraph, at desktop (desktop-04 to desktop-06) and on phone (phone-03, phone-04)
findings.fault: The whole article body is centred. Long paragraphs have a ragged edge on both sides, so the eye has to hunt for the start of every line. In the numbered list, each centred item drifts away from its number. Item 2's text starts far right of its '2.', item 3's sits loose in the middle, and the wrapped lines don't align under the first. The list stops reading as a list, and proximity and continuity between each number and its text break down. On the left, the heading and byline sit flush while the text under them is centred, so the column has no common edge.
findings.who_objects: A development-bank reader reading one of Mark's articles, which the brief calls the product, would tire after a paragraph and lose their place in the list. Angélique would also object, because whatever list or subhead she adds will look as broken as this one.

findings.where: The 'Get Mark's briefings on PPP reform' / Subscribe band directly below the first screen (desktop-02 top; phone-01, straight after the hero action)
findings.fault: A full-width field of saturated house blue with a large centred serif heading and a white button comes straight after the hero. When you squint, this band outweighs the hero's own action, a small blue box on slate. The page now leads with two competing asks, and the louder one is the secondary one. On phone it arrives just below 'Write to me directly', so the two calls to action stack one after the other.
findings.who_objects: A visitor working out how to reach Mark is pulled towards subscribing instead of writing to him. The founder would also object: the brief asks for one message and one quiet action, and this makes the first scroll read like a marketing funnel.

findings.where: Section labels below the fold: 'PALETTE' (desktop-02), 'Type pair' and 'Texture' (desktop-03), 'An article page' (desktop-04), 'Motion sketch' (desktop-06), and the same on phone
findings.fault: Sections of the same rank are labelled in three different ways: blue tracked capitals for Palette, a small bold grey sans for Type pair, An article page and Motion sketch, and a large italic serif heading for Texture. Similarity breaks down, and Texture looks like a higher-ranking section than its neighbours.
findings.who_objects: The founder, reading the specimen as one system, cannot tell whether these labels are meant to differ. It also contradicts the type note on the same page that says 'never tracked capitals'.

findings.where: Article page specimen: the notes about the 32 px rhythm and 'grey for reading, blue only where something can be clicked' (desktop-04 right column; phone-04 after the PDF card)
findings.fault: On desktop, the note floats in the right column next to the article's title and opening paragraph, with no rule or region marking it off. On phone, it falls after the PDF card in the same grey sans as the article's metadata. Nothing groups it apart from the article, so it reads as part of the article itself.
findings.who_objects: The founder judging the article page would read a builder's annotation as if it were article content, which muddies the article as it would look on the live site.

findings.where: First screen: the 'Placeholder: Mark's photo…' caption at the bottom left (desktop-01)
findings.fault: The caption belongs to the photograph on the right, but it sits at the bottom of the left text column, under the action. By proximity it reads as fine print attached to the email button, not as a note on the photo.
findings.who_objects: The founder reviewing the first screen sees a stray line under the action and could take it for small print about contacting Mark.

findings.where: Desktop specimen sections: Texture (desktop-03/04), the article page (desktop-04 to desktop-06) and the Motion sketch left column (desktop-06/07)
findings.fault: Content stops at about the middle of the 1100 px frame and leaves a large empty area. The two Texture photographs fill only the left half, and the article column runs down the left with nothing on the right after the first note. The Motion sketch's left column ends while its right column runs a whole screen further. The sections look unfinished rather than deliberately quiet.
findings.who_objects: The founder scrolling the specimen would see lopsided, half-filled bands and read them as unfinished work, not as restraint.
